subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- November 23, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - November 23, 2026

Our development team has been busy refining the AcreetionOS experience with several key improvements this week. The XLibre desktop environment received a fix for bottom bar icon clickability, ensuring smoother navigation for all users. We also updated Electron to its latest version, bringing enhanced performance and security for new users installing the distribution. These changes reflect our ongoing commitment to delivering a polished Arch-based experience without the usual complexity.

Behind the scenes, our infrastructure got meaningful upgrades with the addition of a backgrounds submodule that tracks our GitLab repository for wallpaper management. The initial commit for acreetionos-wallpapers is now live, giving us a dedicated space to curate and distribute beautiful default backgrounds. Our intelligence sync process has also been enhanced to automatically update the newsletter archive, wiki guides, and feed content, keeping documentation fresh with minimal manual overhead. A CSP fix was deployed to resolve an edge caching issue that affected page-status.js on some CDN nodes.

The blog deployment pipeline received attention with a new build configuration for blog.acreetionos.org that properly sets the SITE variable for GitHub Pages. This ensures our community updates and technical articles publish reliably with each push. Calamares installer work continues steadily as Darren refines the installation experience that greets every new AcreetionOS user. The ISO build pipeline remains stable, producing consistent releases that uphold our repository sovereignty principles.

In broader community news, the LLVM project announced it is wrapping up its significant relicensing effort, a development that impacts the entire open-source compiler ecosystem. This multi-year initiative aims to modernize LLVM's licensing framework while maintaining compatibility with existing projects. The resolution brings clarity for distributions like ours that rely on LLVM toolchains for building and optimizing system packages.

Vim Classic released version 8.3.1 this week, continuing the maintenance of the traditional Vim editor experience that many of our users prefer. This release includes bug fixes and stability improvements that enhance the editing workflow on AcreetionOS systems. The Vim Classic project provides an alternative to the main Vim distribution with a focus on conservative, tested changes that prioritize reliability over new features.

Security updates landed from AlmaLinux on Friday, addressing vulnerabilities in packages including bind9.18, bubblewrap, fence-agents, freerdp, grafana, and several Java and GStreamer components. While AcreetionOS follows Arch's rolling release model
